sections.h2: Which offices run property tax in Adair County, KY?
sections.html:
Adair County divides the job between two offices. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) puts a value on each parcel, and the sheriff takes in the money. The rate itself is voted by the bodies that levy the tax, such as the fiscal court and the school board.

Find the PVA on Public Square in Columbia: 424 Public Square, Suite 2, KY 42728, telephone (270) 384-3673, weekdays eight to four. Deputies there process deed transfers, including partial sales, and adjust vehicle values. On the same contact page the county lists the sheriff at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Every parcel is valued as it stood on January 1, which the state treats as the assessment date. A house bought in February therefore tends to get that year's bill in the seller's name, so an Adair County purchase contract should say who reimburses whom.

sections.h2: When must Adair County tax bills be paid?
sections.html:
The sheriff takes payment through every stage of the statutory calendar in KRS 134.015. The table shows what each stage costs.

Kentucky regular collection schedule for real property (source: KRS 134.015)
Payment windowWhat you owe
On or before November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
After January 31Face amount plus 10 percent

A late mailing can trigger an alternative timetable: a month for the discount, a month at face value and a month at the 5 percent penalty. Bills still open after April 15 are handed to the County Clerk, who records a lien on the parcel.

sections.h2: What would an Adair County owner actually pay?
sections.html:
The state's own rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents the year before. On a house assessed at the county's $150,800 Census median value, that state share alone comes to about $159.85. County, school and district rates are added to it, and the PVA or sheriff can tell you the combined figure for a specific address.

The homestead exemption changes the math for older owners. If the assessment drops to $101,700 after the exemption, the state share falls to about $107.80. Paying early trims 2 percent off whatever the total turns out to be.

Those numbers matter in a sale because the year's bill has to be divided between buyer and seller somewhere. Ask the closing agent how the contract handles it, and ask the sheriff what has already been paid on the account.

sections.h2: How does an Adair County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
An appeal cannot be filed until you have sat down with the PVA or a deputy. The roll lies open to the public for two weeks from the first Monday in May, and a value you dispute is best raised in that period, or sooner once notices are mailed.

  • At the conference the PVA must walk you through how the number was reached, and a written record is made.
  • Lodge the appeal with the County Clerk by the close of the first workday after inspection ends.
  • Gather proof: descriptions of the land and buildings, insurance papers, building costs and comparable listings or sales. Without it the board turns the appeal down.
  • Show up for the hearing a few weeks later. Missing it ends your right to go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

A paid representative has to fall into a listed category, for example an attorney, CPA, licensed broker or certified appraiser, and must bring your written authorization. If the board lands above the figure you claimed, you receive a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Can an older Adair County owner reduce the tax base?
sections.html:
Yes, through the homestead exemption. Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classed as totally disabled, can have a slice of the assessment deducted, which the state Revenue Department fixed at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply that to $150,800, the Census median home value here, and the taxed amount falls to $101,700.

File the form with the Adair County PVA during the year you want relief, by post, fax or email. Age can be shown with a driver's license, Medicare card or birth certificate, and a Kentucky license or state ID proves residence. A household gets one exemption, and one spouse reaching 65 satisfies the age test.

Once approved, the exemption continues while the applicant stays in the home as owner. After a sale, the seller should notify the PVA so it is removed from the old address and can be requested for a new one.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell an Adair County house with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
A delinquent balance does not vanish at closing. State law treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a lien on the parcel stays in force until it is paid or the 11 years in KRS 134.420 expire, even after a transfer. Any title search will turn it up, so get a payoff amount from the sheriff before the house is listed.

Once the clerk holds the bill, interest accrues at 1 percent a month, with commissions for the clerk and the county attorney and a fee to record the lien. The county attorney sends two mailed notices. A sale of the certificates may be set between 90 and 135 days after transfer, and an outside investor who buys one can tack on charges of its own.

Settling with the sheriff ahead of the April 15 transfer keeps the clerk's commissions, monthly interest and lien fee off the account.

sections.h2: What is Adair County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Green County gave up part of its land in 1801 to create Adair County, whose lone municipality, Columbia, serves as seat. Roughly 405 square miles of land lie on the Pennyroyal Plateau, over 40 percent of it wooded. The Green River drains the county, and its impoundment as Green River Lake anchors a state park shared with Taylor County.

Farming drives the local economy: livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco. Road access improved a great deal once the Cumberland Parkway opened in 1973. Students attend Adair County Schools from the primary center to the high school. Census QuickFacts supplies these numbers:

  • 2025 population: 19,423, a gain of 2.8 percent over 2020.
  • Owner-occupied share of housing: 77.2 percent.
  • Home value at the midpoint: $150,800.
  • Midpoint household income: $53,553, and 21.2 percent of residents below the poverty line.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $771.

Neighbors on the map are Green, Taylor, Casey, Russell, Cumberland and Metcalfe counties. Columbia keeps Central time while Taylor and Casey counties to the north run on Eastern, a detail worth remembering when scheduling a closing with out-of-county parties. About 73.5 percent of residents live in rural areas, and the Census counted 7,136 households averaging 2.51 people.

The county recorded just six building permits in 2025, so nearly every sale involves a house that already stands. If a property carries deferred repairs or back taxes, a buyer who purchases as-is for cash can settle both issues in one closing.

faqs.q: When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?
faqs.a: It is November 1. Pay the full bill by then and you keep 2 percent. After that date the bill is due at face value through December 31, with penalties starting in January.

faqs.q: Who takes payment of Adair County tax bills?
faqs.a: Pay the Adair County Sheriff, whom the county lists at (270) 384-2776. The PVA, reachable at (270) 384-3673, only values property and never takes payments.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Adair County?
faqs.a: The amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, as set by the Kentucky Department of Revenue, and it comes off assessed value. Qualifying owners are 65 and over or totally disabled, and they file through the PVA in Columbia.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?
faqs.a: Not after the inspection window closes. A conference with the PVA comes first, then a filing with the County Clerk by the end of the next workday. The window opens the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days.

faqs.q: What happens if Adair County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: The bill moves to the county clerk after April 15 as a certificate of delinquency. A lien is recorded and interest runs at 1 percent a month, and the certificate can be sold 90 to 135 days after the transfer.
